name: GreptimeDB
tagline: Rust observability database that keeps metrics, logs and traces in one columnar engine on object storage.
description: GreptimeDB is an open-source database from Greptime that stores metrics, logs, events and traces in a single columnar engine built on Apache Arrow, DataFusion and Parquet, with compute separated from object storage. It speaks many dialects at once: SQL and PromQL for queries, and Prometheus remote write, InfluxDB line protocol, OpenTelemetry, Elasticsearch bulk, Loki push and the MySQL and PostgreSQL wire protocols for access. That lets one cluster replace several observability backends. It reached 1.0 in April 2026, runs from a single binary at the edge up to Kubernetes clusters, and is sold commercially as GreptimeDB Enterprise and the hosted GreptimeCloud.

pricing.notes: Open source is free; GreptimeCloud is usage-based with a free tier; Enterprise is contract-priced.

scale.notes: Frontend, datanode and metasrv roles scale independently; data lives in object storage with local caches.

strengths: One engine for metrics, logs and traces instead of three backends
Object storage keeps long retention cheap
SQL and PromQL over the same data
Wide protocol compatibility eases migration from Prometheus, InfluxDB, Elasticsearch and Loki
Runs as a single binary on edge devices or as a Kubernetes cluster
weaknesses: Young compared with Prometheus-ecosystem or Elasticsearch stacks
Breadth of protocols means some compatibility edges are thinner than the originals
Smaller community and fewer public large-scale references
Object-storage reads add latency for cold queries
useCases: Unified observability backend for metrics, logs and traces
Edge data collection synced to the cloud
notIdealFor: Teams that need a decade-proven stack
